title: Optimality, uniqueness and stability of Gerver's sofa from one coercive certificate, formalized in Lean 4
summary: The moving sofa problem asks for the largest area of a planar shape that can be moved around the right-angled corner of a hallway of unit width. Jineon Baek proved (arXiv:2411.19826) that Gerver's sofa G, of area 2.2195..., is optimal. His proof bounds the area of every large moving sofa by a concave functional Q of a triple (K, B, D) of convex bodies built from a cap K of the sofa, and shows that Q is largest at Gerver's triple, where it equals |G|. This entry proves one estimate for Q, the coercive certificate, and derives three results from it. On an enlarged domain of triples, on which…
